consolidation.why_one_option: Both PRs relax THE IDENTICAL GATE -- the is_complex(orblock) decline inside rule_block_or (p8_structure/blockaction.rs) and its verbatim twin try_block_or (p8_structure/region_structurer.rs). The shared root cause is Ghidra's BlockBasic::isComplex >2-statement readability budget. They collided hard: both added a CollapseStructure field named condfold_blocks, both added a builder named with_condfold_blocks, condjoin's entry point was even named compute_condfold_blocks, and both bumped the option count 76 -> 77. They differed only in the admission predicate and the value surface.
consolidation.predicate_is_the_union: A sibling is admissible when EITHER rule takes it. Rule A (from #193) is condfold's bounded-prefix rule; Rule B (from #194) is condjoin's statement-shape allowlist. Neither subsumes the other -- each was proven to close a different target -- so they are unioned, not intersected. Rule A is tried first; Rule B is the only rule that admits a nested BlockCondition operand, which is what a guard CASCADE needs.
consolidation.condjoin_disappears: There is no `condjoin` option name, no cond_join Architecture/ArchContext field, no kuna_condjoin.rs, and no second spec section. Exactly ONE net new option: 76 -> 77.

soundness.argument: Rendering-only. BlockGraph::new_block_condition re-parents two existing structuring nodes; no p-code op is moved, reordered, cloned, or deleted. Soundness rests on a precondition rule_block_or already enforces and this option never weakens: orblock.size_in() == 1, so the sibling's statements cannot run on a path where the compound condition is not evaluated. C's short-circuit rule evaluates the right operand exactly when control used to fall into the sibling, and the comma operator is a sequence point, so the absorbed statements still run before the test, in order. The only synthesized operation is negate_condition_rec, a boolean sense flip on an already-computed condition; it is order-neutral.
soundness.proposal_56_worry_does_not_arise: Proposal #56 warned that a wrong de Morgan inversion emits wrong C because the predicates call getuid/geteuid/getegid/getgid, which cannot be reordered past one another. No such reordering is possible: the operands are never swapped, only relabelled. NO PURITY ANALYSIS IS NEEDED. Both original agents and both independent reviewers established this separately.
soundness.is_complex_blast_radius: is_complex() itself was NOT changed. The relaxation is a disjunct at the two rule_block_or/try_block_or call sites only; the other callers (rule_block_while_do and its region_structurer twin) see the unchanged verdict. This is why the 675-assertion corpus is untouched.
new_guards_all_rendering_or_quality: Rule A: orblock must be BlockType::Copy of a single BlockBasic (a BlockList/BlockIf/BlockCondition operand could render braces, multiple lines, or a label inside the parens = invalid C)

Rule A: bounded printed statements (<=5 at on, <=9 at wide) and <=1 statement-root call, counted with the printer's own skip rules (not_printed / markers / implied-out / bare CPUI_BRANCH) so the cap governs exactly what appears
Rule A: no non-terminal branch op (mirrors angr _build_multistatementexpr_statements refusing a non-terminal ConditionalJump or any Jump; a goto is not an expression); must end in CPUI_CBRANCH

Rule B: statement-shape allowlist (marker | op with an output | void CALL/CALLIND | STORE | the single terminal CBRANCH); declines RETURN, a second branch, BRANCHIND, CALLOTHER, and any no-return call
Rule B: <=2 conservatively-scored statements and <=2 calls per block (counting EVERY call, unlike Rule A)
Rule B: a nested BlockCondition operand requires BOTH sub-blocks admissible (not isComplex's getBlock(0)-only delegation), plus <=4 condition leaves and <=4 total scored statements at the fold site
both rules: no instruction comment attached in the block (emit_basic_block_ops suppresses emit_comment_group under comma_separate, so folding would silently DELETE a WARNING: line -- decline instead)
gate: the pre-existing !orblock.is_interior_goto_target() decline is NEVER relaxed (emit_block_copy emits the label statement first, so a labelled sibling would print `label_x:` inside an expression)

gate: a relaxed fold's node is force-marked complex, because BlockCondition::isComplex delegates to sub-block 0 and would otherwise report the LEFT operand's trivial verdict for a node whose right operand is a comma chain, letting rule_block_while_do hoist the whole chain into a while(...) header

1_rule_a_call_cap_semantics.finding: condfold's call cap was documented as `<=1 call` but prefix_eligible's implied-output skip runs before the is_call test, so a call inlined into the condition is never charged. Witness: mv -O2 copy_internal at `wide` renders both cached_umask(...) (counted) and fchmod(...) (not counted).
1_rule_a_call_cap_semantics.decision: KEEP the statement-root semantics; make them unmistakable rather than tighten.
actions: constant renamed MAX_PREFIX_CALLS -> MAX_PREFIX_ROOT_CALLS so the name IS the contract
docs in kuna_condfold.rs, architecture.rs, phases.toml summary/use_when and docs/spec/08-structuring.md all state statement-root counting explicitly and record the decision
1_rule_a_call_cap_semantics.rationale: The cap exists to bound the PRINTED comma chain, which is what harms readability, and printed-statement granularity is the only granularity the structurer can observe cheaply. It is a readability bound, not a soundness bound (the fold moves no p-code and the sequencing argument is independent of the call count), so the looser count cannot produce wrong C. Rule B, which charges every call op (MAX_SHAPE_CALLS), is the tighter half of the union and covers the shapes where call density is the real concern.

2_rule_b_cap_bypass.finding: MAX_CONDJOIN_LEAVES / MAX_CONDJOIN_TOTAL_STMTS were consulted only inside the admission check, which is only reached when is_complex(orblock) is true. Because is_complex(BlockCondition) delegates to getBlock(0) alone, once a fold produced a Condition whose LEFTMOST leaf was non-complex, a later rule_block_or taking that Condition as orblock saw is_complex == false, skipped the check, and the caps never applied to the merged result.
2_rule_b_cap_bypass.action: The main bypass is CLOSED, for free, by inheriting #193's `condfolded` force-complex marking: every relaxed result reports itself complex, so it always re-enters the admission check and the caps always apply to it. #194 had no such marking; the union does.
2_rule_b_cap_bypass.residual_documented_not_hidden: The caps bound the relaxation at each site where it is EXERCISED; they are not a global bound on the final condition's width. A purely upstream-legal fold (both operands non-complex) can still extend a cascade on the LEFT without consulting them -- exactly as it can on main today, and each such leaf is bounded by Ghidra's own two-statement budget. The spec and phases.toml now say this instead of claiming the caps hold unconditionally.

4_comment_loss.finding: The comment guard only sees comments buffered in Funcdata at structuring time; COMMA_SEPARATE suppresses emit_comment_group, so a later-produced advisory can vanish.
4_comment_loss.action: Documented as a known effect in the module docs, architecture.rs, phases.toml use_when and the spec. Not fixed: fixing it would require the structurer to predict comments passes have not produced yet.
4_comment_loss.reproduced_on_this_main: newbury::main -- 4 WARNING comments at off, 3 at on; the lost one is `/* WARNING: branchflip: flipped negated guard for linearity (positive condition, if/else arms swapped) */`. It is a kuna advisory annotation, never a correctness signal, and the emitted C is unaffected.

speed.method: INTERLEAVED on CHILD CPU TIME (user+sys via os.wait4 rusage). scripts.pipeline.timeit times all OFF samples and then all ON samples, so load drift over the run does not cancel; PR #193 recorded +7.9% / +24.1% / +72.0% for the SAME measurement on three consecutive runs of a loaded box. This harness alternates off/on/wide inside each iteration so drift cancels, and CPU time is insensitive to contention. Box load average during measurement: 12-14 (other users' jobs).
speed.honest_reading: On a small function the cost is unmeasurable (<0.5%). On lighttpd main -- a 4-second outlier where the option actually fires several times -- two independent interleaved runs put `on` at +3.4% and +4.8% and `wide` at +2.8% and +0.04%. Since `on` and `wide` emit byte-identical C on this function, the spread between those two `wide` numbers is a direct read of the noise floor (~2.5 points) even on CPU time. The measurement is within the 5% budget but it is NOT tight on this target, and it is stated that way rather than rounded down.
speed.expected_cost: one extra predicate inside the loop that already calls bb_is_complex (skipped entirely when off), plus a set/map lookup at an existing decline, plus the two-rule precompute over the bblocks list. The bigger term on a large function is second-order: more folds mean the fixpoint structuring loop matches more schemas.
speed.note: The option ships default-OFF for readability/presentation reasons, not speed. With it off the precompute is skipped and every gate disjunct is dead.

aggregate_invalid_c_sweep.method: kuna decompile-all --json at off/on/wide over 7 real binaries; every function whose text CHANGED vs off was syntax-checked by wrapping it in a permissive C translation unit and running `gcc -fsyntax-only`. Semantic diagnostics that a decompiled body always produces in a prelude-only TU (undeclared identifier, unknown type name, has no member, argument count, conflicting types, incomplete type, ...) are filtered out; SYNTAX errors are not.

not_closed: Default-ON. That needs its own 0/675 ablation and a DIV row; the 2827-function sweep above is supporting evidence (monotone improvement, no invalid C), not the ablation. The decbench regression and the comment-loss effect are both presentation arguments for staying opt-in.

The `wide` level no longer differentiates itself on any named target on this main. It is retained because it still wins in aggregate (9 gotos, 27 ifs, 146 loc over `on` across 2827 functions), but a future PR could reasonably fold it away.

Rule B's expression-size caps are not a GLOBAL bound on the folded condition's width; a purely upstream-legal fold can extend a cascade on the left without consulting them (documented above and in the spec).
A comment produced by a pass that runs AFTER structuring can still be dropped by the comma_separate operand (documented; newbury::main loses one branchflip advisory).
angr's four schema arms are matched only through Ghidra's ruleBlockOr shape. angr's type_b/type_d (the with-else forms) can fire on graphs ruleBlockOr's topology checks reject; those remain unfolded.
The region structurer still does not fully converge on build_spec_list; making it converge is a separate, larger opportunity.
